questions.q: What does the phase estimation problem ask you to find?
options: The unknown phase θ in U|ψ⟩ = e^(2πiθ)|ψ⟩, given a unitary U and access to its eigenvector |ψ⟩
The full matrix representation of an arbitrary unitary U
A classical factoring algorithm that runs in polynomial time
The number of qubits needed to build any quantum computer
questions.explain: Phase estimation estimates the unknown real phase θ encoded in a unitary's eigenvalue e^(2πiθ), given the ability to apply U to its eigenvector |ψ⟩.

questions.q: Why can't you just diagonalize U as a matrix to find θ classically, for a U acting on many qubits?
options: A unitary on n qubits is a 2^n x 2^n matrix, which becomes impossibly large to even write down for realistic n, and in practice U is given as a procedure, not a matrix of readable entries
Diagonalization is mathematically undefined for unitary matrices
Classical computers cannot represent complex numbers
Eigenvalues only exist for matrices acting on a single qubit
questions.explain: The matrix size grows as 2^n x 2^n, making explicit diagonalization infeasible well before n reaches even modest sizes, and realistic U's are given as circuits or physical processes rather than explicit matrices.

questions.q: What does it mean to treat U as a 'black-box oracle' in the phase estimation setting?
options: You can apply U (and controlled versions of U) to a register, but you never get to inspect U as a matrix
U is a randomly generated matrix with no known structure
U can only be applied once during the entire algorithm
U must be classically simulable before it can be used
questions.explain: The black-box oracle model captures the realistic access pattern: you can call U as an operation, but you don't get to read off its matrix entries directly.

questions.q: Why does θ matter physically in the quantum chemistry use case, where U = e^(iHt) for Hamiltonian H?
options: The eigenvalues of H, recoverable via the phases θ, correspond to the molecule's allowed energy levels, including its ground-state energy
θ has no physical meaning in this context and is purely a mathematical artifact
θ directly gives the number of atoms in the molecule
θ determines only the color of the molecule, not its energy
questions.explain: Because U is the time-evolution operator e^(iHt), its eigenvalues e^(2πiθ) are directly tied to H's eigenvalues -- the system's energy levels -- making θ a physically meaningful quantity.

questions.q: Why is it valid to write every eigenvalue of a unitary U as e^(2πiθ) for real θ, rather than as a general complex number?
options: Unitary operators preserve vector length, so every eigenvalue must have magnitude exactly 1, meaning it lies on the unit circle and can always be written as a pure phase
It is a simplifying assumption that only holds for 2x2 unitaries
Because all eigenvectors of unitaries happen to be real-valued
It is only true when U equals the identity matrix
questions.explain: Unitarity forces every eigenvalue to have magnitude 1, so it can always be represented as e^(2πiθ) for some real θ -- no generality is lost by this notation.
